name: Melatonin
oneLineAnswer: A hormone your body makes in the dark to time sleep; supplements are sold for jet lag and body-clock problems.
whatItDoes: Melatonin is a hormone your brain releases in the dark.
It helps set the timing of your circadian rhythm, the body clock that runs your day.
Your body builds it from the amino acid L-tryptophan.
Light at night can block your body's melatonin production.
Researchers think it has other jobs in the body beyond sleep, but those jobs are not well understood.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Whether melatonin helps chronic insomnia is unclear. Guidelines cited by NCCIH say the evidence is too weak to recommend it.
Long-term safety is unknown, because NCCIH says information on long-term use of melatonin supplements is lacking.
There has been very little research on melatonin use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
The long-term effects of melatonin in children are not well studied.
Evidence about shift workers is weak; the reviews NCCIH cites were small or inconclusive.
Studies of melatonin for cancer symptoms were small and produced mixed results.
The other roles melatonin plays in the body are not fully understood.
Whether melatonin helps with COVID-19 cannot be judged yet, according to NCCIH.
safetyNotes: Melatonin can make you drowsy. One melatonin product label tells people not to drive or use heavy machinery after taking it.
NCCIH says people with epilepsy, and people taking blood thinner medicines, need medical supervision when using melatonin supplements.
Sleep medicine guidelines from 2015 advise against melatonin use by people with dementia, per NCCIH.
Melatonin may stay active longer in older people than in younger people and cause daytime drowsiness.
Supplement labels can be wrong. NCCIH reports a 2017 study where 26 percent of tested melatonin supplements also contained serotonin.

evidence.claim: Melatonin is a hormone the brain produces in response to darkness.
evidence.quote: Melatonin is a hormone that your brain produces in response to darkness.

evidence.claim: Melatonin helps with the timing of circadian rhythms and with sleep.
evidence.quote: It helps with the timing of your circadian rhythms (24-hour internal clock) and with sleep.

evidence.claim: Light exposure at night can block melatonin production.
evidence.quote: Being exposed to light at night can block melatonin production.

evidence.claim: NCCIH states that melatonin's roles beyond sleep are not fully understood.
evidence.quote: Research suggests that melatonin plays other important roles in the body beyond sleep. However, these effects are not fully understood.

evidence.claim: Melatonin supplements can be made from animals or microorganisms, but are usually synthetic.
evidence.quote: Melatonin dietary supplements can be made from animals or microorganisms, but most often they’re made synthetically.

evidence.claim: NCCIH names jet lag and delayed sleep-wake phase disorder among conditions melatonin supplements may help with.
evidence.quote: Melatonin supplements may help with certain conditions, such as jet lag, delayed sleep-wake phase disorder

evidence.claim: Guidelines cited by NCCIH do not recommend melatonin for chronic insomnia because evidence is not strong enough.
evidence.quote: there’s not enough strong evidence on the effectiveness or safety of melatonin supplementation for chronic insomnia to recommend its use

evidence.claim: Short-term melatonin use appears safe for most people, while long-term safety information is lacking.
evidence.quote: Short-term use of melatonin supplements appears to be safe for most people, but information on the long-term safety of supplementing with melatonin is lacking.

evidence.claim: In the United States melatonin is regulated less strictly than a prescription or over-the-counter drug.
evidence.quote: it’s regulated less strictly by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) than a prescription or over-the-counter drug would be

evidence.claim: In several other countries melatonin is sold only with a prescription and treated as a drug.
evidence.quote: In several other countries, melatonin is available only with a prescription and is considered a drug.

evidence.claim: The amount of melatonin in a product often does not match the product label.
evidence.quote: For most of the supplements, the amount of melatonin in the product didn’t match what was listed on the product label.

evidence.claim: NCCIH reports that 26 percent of supplements in a 2017 study also contained serotonin.
evidence.quote: 26 percent of the supplements contained serotonin, a hormone that can have harmful effects even at relatively low levels.

evidence.claim: A 2015 safety review found only mild side effects reported in short-term studies of adults, surgical patients and critically ill patients.
evidence.quote: A 2015 review on the safety of melatonin supplements indicated that only mild side effects were reported in various short-term studies

evidence.claim: Studies of melatonin for shift workers were small or inconclusive.
evidence.quote: studies on whether melatonin supplements help shift workers were generally small or inconclusive

evidence.claim: Studies of melatonin for cancer symptoms were small and had mixed results.
evidence.quote: Studies of the effect of melatonin supplements on cancer symptoms or treatment-related side effects have been small and have had mixed results.

evidence.claim: NCCIH says it is too soon to conclude whether melatonin helps with COVID-19.
evidence.quote: At this point, it is too soon to reach conclusions on whether melatonin is helpful for COVID-19.

evidence.claim: People with epilepsy and people taking blood thinners need medical supervision when using melatonin supplements.
evidence.quote: people with epilepsy and those taking blood thinner medications need to be under medical supervision when taking melatonin supplements

evidence.claim: There is little information on the long-term effects of melatonin in children.
evidence.quote: there’s little information on the long-term effects of melatonin use in children

evidence.claim: NCCIH notes a lack of research on melatonin safety in pregnant or breastfeeding women.
evidence.quote: There’s been a lack of research on the safety of melatonin use in pregnant or breastfeeding women.

evidence.claim: Melatonin may stay active longer in older people and cause daytime drowsiness.
evidence.quote: Melatonin may stay active in older people longer than in younger people and cause daytime drowsiness.

evidence.claim: The 2015 American Academy of Sleep Medicine guidelines recommend against melatonin use by people with dementia.
evidence.quote: The 2015 guidelines by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine recommend against melatonin use by people with dementia.

evidence.claim: PubChem's compound description calls melatonin a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in humans.
evidence.quote: It is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in humans.

evidence.claim: PubChem's pharmacology section says melatonin is produced in the pineal gland, released into the blood, and that darkness stimulates its production while light inhibits it.
evidence.quote: It helps regulate sleep-wake cycles or the circadian rhythm. Production of melatonin is stimulated by darkness and inhibited by light.

evidence.claim: PubChem's pharmacology section says the amino acid L-tryptophan is a precursor in melatonin synthesis.
evidence.quote: The essential amino acid L-tryptophan is a precursor in the synthesis of melatonin.

evidence.claim: PubChem records melatonin's molecular formula as C13H16N2O2 and its molecular weight as 232.28.
evidence.quote: "MolecularFormula": "C13H16N2O2", "MolecularWeight": "232.28"

evidence.claim: An openFDA label for a product listing melatonin warns that long-term use has not been studied and that it may cause drowsiness.
evidence.quote: Long-term use of melatonin has not been studied. May cause drowsiness. Do not use before or while operating a motor vehicle or heavy machinery.

evidence.claim: That same melatonin label states its claims rest on homeopathic practice and were not accepted as medical evidence or evaluated by the FDA.
evidence.quote: Claims based on traditional homeopathic practice, not accepted medical evidence. Not FDA evaluated.

evidence.claim: openFDA labels record the UNII code JL5DK93RCL for the substance melatonin.
evidence.quote: "unii": [ "JL5DK93RCL" ]

evidence.claim: A DailyMed label search for melatonin returned 60 records, and the first page consisted of multi-ingredient products that include melatonin.
evidence.quote: "total_elements": 60

evidence.claim: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 1,089 registered studies matching the term Melatonin.
evidence.quote: "totalCount": 1089

evidence.claim: Registered trials on ClinicalTrials.gov include studies of melatonin and light treatment for jet lag and sleep disorders.
evidence.quote: Effectiveness of Combining Light and Non-Light Treatments for Jet Lag and Sleep Disorders

gaps: The NCCIH page could not be read by a plain HTTP fetch: it returns a JavaScript shell made mostly of stylesheet code. I read the rendered page in a browser tab instead, so the NCCIH quotes come from the rendered text of the same URL.

openFDA labels naming melatonin are homeopathic or multi-ingredient products. I could not ground FDA-approved indications, standard product strengths, or prescription status for plain melatonin from labels.

No MedlinePlus health topic page dedicated to melatonin was found. MedlinePlus drug monographs are copyrighted and were deliberately not fetched, so no facts come from them. I did fetch the MedlinePlus Insomnia health topic, which does not mention melatonin, so it supports no melatonin claim.
The Internet Archive was offline when I tried it, so no archived snapshot of the NCCIH page could be used as a fallback.

PubChem's pharmacology text aggregates third-party sources rather than a public-domain label, so the receptor and pharmacokinetic details were not used beyond the pineal gland, darkness and tryptophan facts.
I could not ground amounts used in food, natural blood levels, or any no-effect level from the sources I fetched, so the record reports no numbers for those.
